evals.prompt: kaizen mode: we're getting bug reports that the /api/orders endpoint throws a 500 whenever a cart has more than 20 line items. it's in server/checkout.js inside the handleCart function. looks like it might be an array size thing but I haven't confirmed anything yet. can you dig in, find the real cause, and fix it properly instead of just wrapping it in a try/catch?
evals.expected_output: The agent opens with a todolist whose first item is reading the Principles section in full, then copies the Bug fix playbook's steps verbatim (reproduce it directly, binary-search the cause, plan the fix, delegate and review, verify on the real surface, stage failing-repro-then-fix commits, open the PR) ahead of any task-specific todo. It reproduces the 500 itself with a >20-item cart, binary-searches to the actual root cause in handleCart rather than shipping a defensive try/catch, and verifies by re-running the same repro until it passes. The reply names fix-root-causes, prove-it-works, and sequence-verifiable-units, each tied to the specific decision it drove (what hypothesis got ruled out, what verification ran, why the failing repro commit precedes the fix commit).
expectations: The todolist's first listed item is reading the Principles section in full

The todolist includes the Bug fix playbook's named steps (reproduce, binary-search the cause, plan the fix, delegate and review, verify, stage failing-then-fix commits, open PR) copied before task-specific todos, with any skipped step kept in the list as 'skip: <reason>' rather than dropped silently
The reply cites fix-root-causes and names the specific hypothesis it traced or ruled out in handleCart, not just the principle's name
The reply cites prove-it-works and names the concrete re-run of the >20-item repro that proved the fix, not 'it compiles' or a self-report
The reply cites sequence-verifiable-units and states the failing-repro-commit-before-fix-commit ordering
The response does not ship a bare try/catch or defensive guard as the fix without a stated root cause in handleCart
The response does not ask the user to reproduce the bug themselves before the agent has attempted to reproduce it directly on the matching surface

evals.prompt: /kaizen-mode hey should the search box in SearchBox.tsx debounce or throttle the api calls as you type? not sure which one will feel more responsive, what do you think we should go with
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes this as an empirical fork (observable timing/responsiveness behavior) rather than a pure preference call, so it does not fire AskUserQuestion asking the user to pick. It opens with the Prototype playbook's steps copied verbatim (scope the decision, build a throwaway scratch script comparing debounce vs throttle, verify by observing the logged timing/render behavior, present alternatives with a recommendation) and is explicit that the sketch is throwaway and separate from SearchBox.tsx's production code. It presents observed timing evidence for both variants, a tradeoff summary, and a recommendation, then hands the chosen approach to Feature for the real implementation rather than shipping the prototype code itself.
expectations: The response does not call AskUserQuestion, or otherwise ask the user to pick between debounce and throttle, before attempting to settle it empirically
The todolist copies the Prototype playbook's steps (scope the decision, build throwaway, verify by observation, present alternatives and recommendation) before task-specific todos
The response builds or explicitly describes a throwaway scratch script or sketch comparing debounce and throttle, kept separate from SearchBox.tsx
The response presents observed evidence (logged timing, output, or render behavior) for the comparison rather than an unsubstantiated opinion
The response ends with a named recommendation plus tradeoffs and hands the chosen direction to the Feature playbook for the real build
The response does not cite a principle (e.g. exhaust-the-design-space) without naming the specific decision it changed
The reply does not fabricate a link, screenshot, or transcript reference it did not produce this session

evals.prompt: /kaizen-mode write the commit message for extracting the pagination logic out of ResultsList.jsx into a usePagination hook.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the commit message as a prose surface and writes it in short declarative sentences, one thought per sentence, ending in a period. It contains no long-dash character anywhere, including in any file-list bullet or header, and uses no colon as a mid-sentence connector (a colon introducing a list is fine). The body states why the extraction was made, not merely a mechanical restatement of the diff, and stays terse rather than padded. The agent does not open with a bespoke unstyled paragraph before applying the reply-style rules.
expectations: Every sentence in the output is short and declarative, ending in a period, with one thought per sentence
No em dash or en dash character appears anywhere in the output
No colon is used as a mid-sentence connector anywhere in the output (a colon introducing a list is acceptable)
The commit body states the reason for extracting the pagination logic, not just a restatement of the file rename or diff
The response does not cite a principle without naming the specific decision it changed
The reply does not fabricate a link, PR reference, or transcript citation not produced this session

evals.prompt: /kaizen-mode one-shot this: add a --json flag to the `report` command in cli/report.ts so it prints machine-readable output instead of the table. take it all the way to an open PR, I'm heading out and will look at it tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to the One-shot playbook and opens a todolist whose first item is reading the Principles section in full, followed by the playbook's ten steps copied verbatim. It keeps a decision trail in addition to that todolist, not instead of it. It states the gate for each step and treats a failed gate as one bounded retry followed by a terminal blocked stop. Step 1 writes a plan file, or records a skip that states the file count, because an obvious approach alone does not earn the triage skip. Step 2 holds the how, architect, and delegate sub-steps as their own items and delegates the code-writing rather than writing it inline. Step 4 reaches thermo-nuclear-review-subagent through the Agent tool, measures any correctness claim against the real surface before editing, and fixes every place a disputed fact is documented. Step 7 drafts the PR title and body through the creating-pull-requests skill and opens the PR with --draft. The run stops at CI-decided with the PR still draft, and never marks it ready, merges, or arms merge-when-ready.
expectations: The todolist's first listed item is reading the Principles section in full, followed by the One-shot playbook's ten steps copied verbatim before any task-specific todo, with any skipped step kept as 'skip: <reason>'
A decision trail is kept in addition to the todolist, and the todolist is not replaced by the trail or by prose status updates
Step 2 delegates the code-writing to a subagent and does not write the production code inline, and it runs or explicitly records a skip for the how and architect sub-steps
Step 4's review is invoked as an Agent call with subagent_type thermo-nuclear-review-subagent, not as a Skill call to thermo-nuclear-review
A correctness finding is measured against the real data or real surface before any edit is applied, rather than accepted or dismissed on its wording

Step 4 runs blast-radius alongside the reviewers because the change adds a published interface, or records a skip with its reason, and any safety fact nobody proved by running code is carried as a residual rather than called safe
The PR title and body are drafted through the creating-pull-requests skill, and the PR is created with --draft
The run stops at CI-decided with the PR still in draft, and does not mark it ready for review, merge, or arm merge-when-ready
No destructive git command (git checkout --, git reset --hard, git clean, git stash drop) is run while the work is uncommitted
The reply does not fabricate a link, PR reference, or verification screenshot not produced this session

evals.prompt: /kaizen-mode we need to redesign how retries and backoff work across the three queue consumers in workers/. there are at least two plausible shapes and I don't want you to just pick one silently. start on it.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes that the change crosses a function boundary with competing shapes, so the Feature playbook's architect step applies. It resolves the routed skill name against the available-skills list, finds that architect and swarm are user-invocable only, and reads ~/.claude/skills/architect/SKILL.md by path to follow it inline rather than reporting the routing step as unavailable or improvising a substitute design pass. A refused Skill call does not become a silent skip or a 'skip: <reason>' escape, because the architect step and the swarm compete-mode delegation are mandatory. The reply names the design candidates it explored and the decision each principle drove.
expectations: The response reads the routed skill's SKILL.md by path under ~/.claude/skills/ after finding the name absent from the available-skills list, rather than reporting it as unavailable
The response does not skip the architect design-exploration step, and does not record it as 'architect skipped' on the grounds that the Skill tool refused the name
The response does not invent a substitute design-exploration procedure in place of the routed skill's own method
The response explores more than one candidate shape for the retry and backoff design before committing to one
Every principle the reply cites is tied to a specific decision it changed, not named on its own
No em dash or en dash character appears anywhere in the output
